title: Levothyroxine use in the United States, 2008-2018
authors: Brito JP, Ross JS, El Kawkgi OM, Maraka S, Deng Y, Shah ND, et al.
population: Commercially insured and Medicare Advantage enrollees in the US who newly started levothyroxine between 2008 and 2018
funder: This work was supported by the Mayo Clinic Robert D. and Patricia E. Kern Center for the Science of Health Care Delivery, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota. The funder had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: Dr Ross reported grants from the US Food and Drug Administration, Johnson & Johnson, the Medical Device Innovation Consortium, AHRQ, NIH and the Laura and John Arnold Foundation outside the submitted work; Dr Shah reported research support from the FDA, CMS, AHRQ, NHLBI, the National Science Foundation, the Medical Device Innovation Consortium and PCORI; Dr Lipska reported grants from NIDDK and PCORI and support from CMS.
result: Median TSH at initiation was 5.8 mIU/l in 2008 and 5.3 in 2018 (P = .79). Among 58,706 starters with TSH and free or total T4 available, levothyroxine was started for overt hypothyroidism in 4948 (8.4%), subclinical hypothyroidism in 35,814 (61.0%) and normal thyroid function in 17,944 (30.5%), without significant change over the decade except a rise in overt (7.6% to 8.4%) and a fall in severe subclinical hypothyroidism (2.5% to 1.3%).
